messages:
Infra Bot: ALERT: 5xx spike + DNS NXDOMAIN surge in eu-west-1 region. Pager: sara.oncall triggered. summary: 13% error rate last 5m, increased latency for geo-routed endpoints.
Sara (oncall): Seeing same. grafana link -> https://grafana/redwood/d/xx/dns-views (p95 DNS latency up, NXDOMAIN rate jump).
Sara (oncall): initial triage: looks like GeoDNS answers are inconsistent between Cloudflare resolver layer and our Route53 fallback. Some clients getting NXDOMAIN, others getting A-records.
Mike (sre): noted. Started running resolver probes from multiple regions. Results: eu-west resolvers returning NXDOMAIN for service.example.com from some ASes.
Nina (network): cc @sara.oncall @mike.sre — Cloudflare health checks show intermittent 5xx to origin for eu cluster ~12:27 UTC. Route53 health checks still green but responses differ in RRset ordering/TTL.
Chris (eng): Any recent deploys for DNS config / GeoDNS entries?
Deploy Bot: deploys: 1) infra/dns/geo-weights v2026.02.11 (rolled 11:50 UTC) 2) api-backend v3.4.2 (rolled 12:10 UTC)
Sara (oncall): @chris not aware of manual changes. Could be propagation from weigh change. Mike can you run a selective failover?
Mike (sre): Starting targeted mitigation: shift eu traffic to secondary provider (Cloudflare-only routing) via emergency weight change in geo controller. Command: kubectl -n infra exec geo-controller -- curl -XPOST \"http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1/override\" -d '{"region":"eu","policy":"prefer-provider-b"}'
Mike (sre): Doing it now...
Infra Bot: ACTION: geo-controller override applied by mike.sre at 1965432175.
Sara (oncall): After override: observing drop in NXDOMAIN from 13% -> 4% in 90s. Good. Still seeing tail errors from certain ISPs.
Aisha (support): Customers reporting 502s in EU dashboard. Which customers impacted?
Chris (eng): Quick customer impact check: top 5 tenants with errors: acme-corp (12% of their requests), shoply (8%), test-plug (5%). Most are EU-edge heavy.
Nina (network): Root cause hypothesis: GeoDNS RRset fanout mismatch combined with stale resolver caches. We updated weight entries earlier; Route53 had TTL 300 but Cloudflare had a cached negative response and some resolvers honored NXDOMAIN longer due to negative caching (SOA/negative TTL).
Mike (sre): Evidence: dig +trace from 3 EU vantage points shows differing SOA serials and NXDOMAIN responses. Logs: \n```\n;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345\n;; flags: qr aa rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1\n;; AUTHORITY SECTION:\nexample.com.  60 IN SOA ns-1.example.com. hostmaster.example.com. 2026021101 7200 3600 1209600 300\n```\nand from another resolver: \n```\n;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 67890\n```\nMike (sre): Mitigations applied: 1) geo-controller override to prefer Cloudflare (done). 2) lowered Route53 TTLs for critical records to 60s (change batch submitted). 3) bump SOA serial to force negative cache expiry propagation.
Sara (oncall): Mike, paste the aws cli change command you used for Route53 so we can audit.
Mike (sre): Command used: \n```\naws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z1234567890 --change-batch file://route53-lower-ttl.json\n```\nroute53-lower-ttl.json contents: \n```\n{\n  \"Comment\": \"emergency lower TTL\",\n  \"Changes\": [\n    {\"Action\":\"UPSERT\",\"ResourceRecordSet\":{\"Name\":\"service.example.com.\",\"Type\":\"A\",\"TTL\":60,\"ResourceRecords\":[{\"Value\":\"10.0.0.5\"}]}}\n  ]\n}\n```\nMike (sre): Also used Cloudflare API to purge negative cached responses for the zone: \n```\ncurl -X POST \"https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/<ZONE>/purge_cache\" \\ \n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $CF_API_TOKEN\" \\ \n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\ \n --data '{\"files\":[\"https://service.example.com/\"]}'\n```\nNina (network): After purges + TTL reduction the NXDOMAIN rate fell further to ~1.2% in eu-west. Latency p95 still elevated for a subset; likely resolver-level caching in ISPs that respect negative TTLs longer.
Aisha (support): Communicating to affected customers now with status update. Draft: \"We're aware of intermittent DNS failures affecting EU traffic; mitigation in progress, routing shifted to alternate provider, ETA for full recovery ~30-60m.\" 
Chris (eng): Can we confirm origin health? CF health checks intermittent earlier — we saw increased 5xx from origin pool eu instances. Eng teams investigating backend CPU/connection saturation.
Sara (oncall): Assigning chris.eng to lead backend probe. @mike.sre continue monitoring DNS fanout and keep TTL low until we confirm stable answer convergence.
Mike (sre): Will do. I scheduled active probes from 6 vantage points every 30s and set an alert if NXDOMAIN > 2% for 5m.
Deploy Bot: deploy status: no new infra changes since override.
Chris (eng): Quick update: found connection pool exhaustion on api-eu-03 causing 502s, restarting service on node, respawning pods with increased ulimit. Rolling restart now.
Sara (oncall): Good. Any customer-visible improvement post-restart?
Aisha (support): Reports from customers show error reduction around 1965432300 (node restart complete). Support posting updates to tickets.
Mike (sre): By 1965432350 overall NXDOMAIN <0.5%, 5xx errors from EU backends down to baseline. Rolling metrics look stable.
Sara (oncall): Preparing incident severity and initial postmortem notes. Impact: partial DNS resolution failures for EU region for ~35 minutes, peak 13% error rate, mitigated by GeoDNS override and Route53 TTL change + Cloudflare purge; backend restart fixed origin 5xx. Potential contributing factors: TTL/negative caching mismatch, recent geo-weight change earlier today, and transient origin instability.
Chris (eng): Action items: (1) add automated SOA bump if negative cache spike detected, (2) add canary health check to detect RRset divergence between DNS providers, (3) increase connection pool headroom for EU api nodes, (4) docs for emergency geo-controller override.
Sara (oncall): Handoff to night oncall @mike.sre in 15m. Summary for handoff (one-liner): GeoDNS inconsistent RRset + stale negative caches caused partial EU DNS failures; mitigated via provider-prefer override, TTL reduction, cache purge, and backend restart.
Mike (sre): I'll take it. Will keep geo override in place until we confirm stable for 24h and then roll back during low traffic window.
Aisha (support): Sending final customer update now.
Sara (oncall): Closing incident channel for active coordination. Will create incident postmortem ticket with logs and timeline. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
summary: Partial EU DNS resolution failure due to RRset divergence and negative caching; mitigations: geo override, TTL reduction, Cloudflare purge, backend restart; impact: ~35m, peak 13% errors; follow-ups assigned.
